text:
This is Alex Ovechkin's last season, and the farewells have started. The Lightning gave him custom "hot stick" cigars before his final game in Tampa, per NHL.com, and the Capitals' Mentors' Trip was, in Yahoo Sports' words, emotional. Every road game from here has a little of that feeling.

The hockey hasn't matched the mood lately. Washington has lost three straight, outscored 17-8, and the chances say it's real: 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games, including a home-and-home sweep by New Jersey. For the season the Capitals are 10-9-0 and right where their expected points say they belong, a 49% team overall but 53% at five on five, with a power play that produces just 0.51 expected goals a game. Charlie Lindgren is at .851 over his last five starts, 3.8 goals below expected.

Two hits have dominated the headlines. Tom Wilson avoided a suspension for a hit on Sandis Vilmanis, which Florida Hockey Now called wrong, and Jakob Chychrun's hit on Ottawa's Nick Cousins has drawn days of fallout. Wilson, meanwhile, has two points in his last ten games against 5.5 expected. The brightest spot is Cole Hutson, the young defenseman Capitals Outsider says is piling up points. Our playoff odds are 43%. The question is how much of Ovechkin's last lap includes April.
